item.title: PNC provides opportunity for new and experienced Flying Fijians - Seruvakula
Navua focuses on discipline and finishing ahead of FMF IDC
item.description: Navua FC coach Rodeck Singh says the team is focused on improving its discipline and finishing as it prepares for the FMF Inter District Championship. Singh says the team has learned important lessons from its recent BOG campaign and does not want a repeat of what happened during the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
Navua FC coach Rodeck Singh says the team is focused on improving its discipline and finishing as it prepares for the FMF Inter District Championship.

Singh says the team has learned important lessons from its recent BOG campaign and does not want a repeat of what happened during the tournament.

He says discipline will be a major focus, with the team determined not to lose players to red cards, particularly at crucial stages of the tournament.

Singh says the team is also working on its transition play and finishing after missing several scoring opportunities during the BOG.

He says the players are working to sharpen their finishing and ensure they are more clinical in front of goal.

Singh says Navua currently has no major injury concerns and hopes the team remains injury-free throughout the tournament.

He is also calling on Navua supporters to come out in numbers and back the team during the competition.

Navua is in Pool B of the Super Premier Division alongside Ba, Lautoka and Nadi.

The FMF IDC will be held from 6th to 11th October.

item.title: Tailevu aim to bounce back against Suva
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 21/09/2026 The Tailevu Rugby team will regroup as they prepare to take on Suva in this week’s Skipper Cup competition.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 21/09/2026

The Tailevu Rugby team will regroup as they prepare to take on Suva in this week’s Skipper Cup competition.

Tailevu were one of two teams yet to lose a match this season, but that unbeaten run came to an end when they went down 27-22 to Lautoka at Ratu Cakobau Park last Saturday.

Team Manager Pita Naidrolevu says it was not the result they wanted, but they will use the loss as a learning experience for the rest of the season.

He says they will review their game against Lautoka and work on areas that need improvement before facing Suva.

In this week’s matches, Tailevu will meet Suva, Taveuni will host Lautoka, Nadroga will face Naitasiri, Kadavu will take on Navosa, while Malolo will face Nadi.

All matches will be held on Saturday at 3pm.

item.title: 29 athletes and officials to represent Fiji at Youth Olympic Games next month
item.description: Team Fiji will travel to Dakar, Senegal, with a 29-member delegation for the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, with athletes set to compete across six sports. The final delegation was announced during a press conference at the FASANOC office this morning, as Team Fiji enters its final preparation phase ahead of the Games next month.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji will travel to Dakar, Senegal, with a 29-member delegation for the 2026 Youth Olympic Games, with athletes set to compete across six sports.

The final delegation was announced during a press conference at the FASANOC office this morning, as Team Fiji enters its final preparation phase ahead of the Games next month.

The 29-member delegation will represent Fiji in athletics, 3x3 basketball, boxing, futsal, swimming and triathlon.

Team Fiji 3x3 basketball coach Earl Hughes says the Games present a significant opportunity for the players, who are focused on taking each opportunity as it comes.

Hughes says while the team wants to win every game, the immediate focus is on preparing well and executing what they have been working on.

He says the players are excited about representing Fiji at their first Youth Olympic Games and are determined to make the most of the opportunity.

Meanwhile, Team Fiji futsal coach Jose Gerardo says the women's national team has been selected following opportunities to assess players through the national women’s futsal league.

Gerardo says the players have contributed to the development of women’s futsal and have impressed him through their performances both indoors and outdoors.

He says he believes he has selected the best available players to represent Fiji and hopes they can bring joy and hope to fans back home.

Gerardo acknowledges that selecting a squad can come with challenges, but says he has confidence in the group chosen for the Youth Olympic Games.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar from October 30th to November 14th.

item.title: Flying Fijians to drop to 10th in World Rugby rankings after Japan loss
item.description: The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will drop from ninth to 10th in the World Rugby rankings after losing 20-15 to Japan in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final. Fiji entered the tournament with high expectations, hoping to finish their campaign by lifting the Pacific Nations Cup trophy.
item.content:encoded:
The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will drop from ninth to 10th in the World Rugby rankings after losing 20-15 to Japan in the Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup final.

Fiji entered the tournament with high expectations, hoping to finish their campaign by lifting the Pacific Nations Cup trophy.

Instead, Japan produced a determined performance in the final, leaving the Fijian side facing not only the disappointment of missing out on the title but also a drop in the World Rugby rankings.

The defeat will see Fiji slip to 10th in the rankings, while Japan’s victory will give the Brave Blossoms a significant boost.
